key_insight: The paper introduces a physical-constraint-preserving limiter for high-order relativistic hydrodynamics that enforces positive density/pressure and subluminal velocity by turning nonlinear admissibility conditions into small eigenvalue problems.
engineering_relevance: This provides a robust way to run high-order shock-capturing simulations in special relativistic flows without numerical breakdown near strong discontinuities.
method: Uses a GQL reformulation to convert relativistic physical constraints into linear inequalities.
Adds a Zalesak-type flux-corrected transport update to finite-difference WENO schemes.
Computes optimal limiter parameters non-iteratively via stereographic parameterization and small symmetric eigenproblems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive tests from 1D to 3D, including ultra-relativistic Riemann problems and astrophysical jets, showing stable constraint enforcement and design-order accuracy on smooth solutions.
watch_item: The multidimensional relaxation variants reduce cost, but practical efficiency and implementation complexity may still depend on repeatedly solving small eigenproblems and integrating the limiter into existing codes.
paper_title: GQL-Based Physical-Constraint-Preserving High-Order Finite Difference Schemes for Special Relativistic Hydrodynamics in Arbitrary Dimensions
